input_messages.content: Hi there. I’m having trouble sending those picture messages—MMS, I think they’re called—from my phone. It’s been a few hours now and nothing seems to go through. Can you help me fix this?
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that’s enough to get started.
Yes, it’s the number I gave you—555-123-2002—that’s having the problem with sending picture messages.
Looking at the top of my phone, I see signal bars and it says 5G up there. There’s also something that looks like a little data symbol. Does that mean my mobile data is on?

I’m not really sure what APN or Wi-Fi Calling are, and I get a bit lost with permissions. Could you please walk me through what I need to do, step by step? I just want to make sure I don’t mess anything up.
I checked, and it looks like there is an APN called “internet” and the MMSC field has something in it: “http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc.” Is that what it’s supposed to look like?
I checked, and it looks like Wi-Fi Calling is already turned off on my phone. What should I try next?
I checked the permissions for my messaging app, and it looks like it only has permission for “phone.” I don’t see anything about “Storage” or “SMS” being allowed. Could that be causing the problem?
I was able to turn on both the “Storage” and “SMS” permissions for my messaging app, but I still can’t send picture messages. Is there something else I should try? This is getting a bit frustrating.
Alright, I restarted my phone like you said, but I still can’t send picture messages. Is there anything else we can try? I’m starting to worry I’ll never get this working again.

I followed your instructions and reset the APN settings, then restarted my phone again, but I still can’t send picture messages. Is there anything else we can try? I’m really starting to get worried this won’t ever work.
Oh, I see! I didn’t realize I’d gone over my data. Let’s go ahead and add 2GB, please. I just want to be able to send my pictures again. Will this fix it right away?
I just tried, and it looks like I can send picture messages again now! Thank you so much for your help. I was really worried, but I’m glad it’s working.
Thank you so much for your patience and help. I really appreciate it. Have a wonderful day! ###STOP###

user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

messages.content: Hi! How can I help you today?
Hi there. I’m having trouble sending those picture messages—MMS, I think they’re called—from my phone. It’s been a few hours now and nothing seems to go through. Can you help me fix this?

I can help you with your MMS (picture messaging) issue. To get started, I’ll need to identify your account. Could you please provide one of the following:

- The phone number associated with your account,
- Your full name and date of birth (YYYY-MM-DD format), or
- Your customer ID (if you have it)?

Once I have this information, I can begin troubleshooting the problem for you.
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that’s enough to get started.

Thank you for providing your information. I’ve identified your account. To help you with your MMS issue, I’ll need to check a few things about your line and device settings.

Could you please confirm which phone number (if you have more than one) is having trouble sending MMS, or is it the number you provided (555-123-2002)? Once confirmed, I’ll guide you through some quick checks and steps to resolve the issue.
Yes, it’s the number I gave you—555-123-2002—that’s having the problem with sending picture messages.

Thank you for confirming. To troubleshoot your MMS issue, I’ll guide you through a few quick checks on your phone. 

First, could you please check if you have cellular service and mobile data enabled? On your phone, look at the status bar at the top of your screen and let me know if you see signal bars and a data indicator (like 4G, LTE, or 5G). 

If you’re not sure, I can walk you through how to check this on your device. Would you like step-by-step instructions?
Status Bar: 📶³ Good | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Looking at the top of my phone, I see signal bars and it says 5G up there. There’s also something that looks like a little data symbol. Does that mean my mobile data is on?

Yes, seeing signal bars and a “5G” indicator means you have cellular service and your mobile data is likely enabled. That’s a good sign!

Next, let’s check a few more things that can affect MMS:

1. Sometimes, incorrect network settings (APN) can cause MMS issues.
2. If you’re using Wi-Fi Calling, it can sometimes interfere with sending picture messages.
3. The messaging app needs the right permissions to send MMS.

Would you like me to guide you through checking your APN settings, Wi-Fi Calling status, and messaging app permissions? This will help us pinpoint and fix the issue.

I’m not really sure what APN or Wi-Fi Calling are, and I get a bit lost with permissions. Could you please walk me through what I need to do, step by step? I just want to make sure I don’t mess anything up.

Absolutely, I’ll guide you step by step and keep things simple. Let’s start by checking your APN (Access Point Name) settings, which are important for sending MMS.

On your phone, please follow these steps:

1. Open your phone’s “Settings” app.
2. Tap on “Network & Internet” or “Connections” (the exact name may vary).
3. Tap on “Mobile Network.”
4. Look for “Access Point Names” or “APN.”
5. Tap on it and check if there’s an APN listed. If you see one, tap on it and look for a field called “MMSC” or “MMS Center.” 

Let me know if you see an MMSC or if you’re unsure about any of these steps. If you don’t see an MMSC or if the field is blank, let me know—that could be the cause of the problem, and I’ll guide you on how to reset your APN settings safely.

Current APN Name: internet
MMSC URL (for picture messages): http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc
(These are technical settings, usually best left unchanged.)
I checked, and it looks like there is an APN called “internet” and the MMSC field has something in it: “http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc.” Is that what it’s supposed to look like?

Thank you for checking! Yes, having an APN called “internet” and an MMSC field filled in (like “http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc”) is a good sign. That means your APN settings are likely correct.

Next, let’s check if Wi-Fi Calling is enabled, as it can sometimes interfere with sending MMS. Here’s how you can check:

1. Go to your phone’s “Settings.”
2. Tap on “Network & Internet” or “Connections.”
3. Look for “Wi-Fi Calling.”
4. See if it’s turned ON or OFF.

Please let me know if Wi-Fi Calling is ON. If it is, I’ll guide you on how to turn it OFF temporarily to see if that resolves your MMS issue. If you don’t see the option or it’s already OFF, let me know as well.
Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned OFF.
I checked, and it looks like Wi-Fi Calling is already turned off on my phone. What should I try next?

Great, thanks for checking that. Since your APN settings and Wi-Fi Calling both look fine, the next thing to check is whether your messaging app has the necessary permissions to send MMS.

Could you please check the app permissions for your messaging app? Here’s how:

1. Open your phone’s “Settings.”
2. Tap on “Apps” or “Applications.”
3. Find and tap on your messaging app (it might be called “Messages” or “Messaging”).
4. Tap on “Permissions.”
5. Make sure that permissions for “Storage” and “SMS” are enabled.

Let me know if either of these permissions is missing or turned off. If you’re not sure, just let me know what you see, and I’ll help you interpret it.
The following apps are installed on the phone: messaging, browser
App 'messaging' has permission for: phone.
I checked the permissions for my messaging app, and it looks like it only has permission for “phone.” I don’t see anything about “Storage” or “SMS” being allowed. Could that be causing the problem?

Yes, that could definitely be causing the problem. Your messaging app needs both “Storage” and “SMS” permissions to send and receive MMS (picture messages).

Please enable both “Storage” and “SMS” permissions for your messaging app:

1. In the permissions screen for your messaging app, look for “Storage” and “SMS.”
2. Tap on each one and select “Allow.”

If you don’t see them listed, there may be an option like “Add permissions” or “See all permissions.” Once you’ve enabled both, try sending a picture message again.

Let me know if you’re able to enable those permissions and if sending MMS works afterward. If you need help finding the options, just let me know what you see on your screen.

Success. Permission 'storage' granted to app 'messaging'.
Status Bar: 📶³ Good | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

Success. Permission 'sms' granted to app 'messaging'.
Status Bar: 📶³ Good | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
I was able to turn on both the “Storage” and “SMS” permissions for my messaging app, but I still can’t send picture messages. Is there something else I should try? This is getting a bit frustrating.

Thank you for updating the permissions, and I understand how frustrating this can be. Let’s try another important step: restarting your phone. Sometimes, changes to permissions or network settings only take effect after a reboot.

Please restart your device by powering it off and then turning it back on. After your phone restarts, try sending a picture message again.

Let me know if this helps, or if the issue persists. If it still doesn’t work, we’ll continue troubleshooting together.

Restarting network services...

Alright, I restarted my phone like you said, but I still can’t send picture messages. Is there anything else we can try? I’m starting to worry I’ll never get this working again.

Thank you for your patience. Let’s try resetting your APN settings, as sometimes even a small error in these settings can prevent MMS from working, even if they look correct.

Here’s how to reset your APN settings:

1. Go to your phone’s “Settings.”
2. Tap on “Network & Internet” or “Connections.”
3. Tap on “Mobile Network.”
4. Tap on “Access Point Names” or “APN.”
5. Look for an option like “Reset to default” or “Reset settings” (usually found in the menu or at the bottom of the screen).
6. Confirm the reset if prompted.

After resetting your APN settings, please restart your phone again. Once your phone is back on, try sending a picture message.

Let me know if you’re able to reset the APN settings and if this resolves the issue. If not, we’ll continue to help you until it’s fixed.
